leads.summary: D-Bus-activatable desktop entries do not inherit the helper's SHELL override
leads.consequence: On a session bus with a DBusActivatable=true desktop entry, gtk-launch delegates through GIO's org.freedesktop.Application Activate/Open D-Bus method instead of spawning Exec from its own environment. GIO's platform data includes activation/startup tokens, not SHELL. If the user manager's D-Bus activation environment still has Bash after chsh to Zsh, launching the installed Files (Nautilus) entry from Apps does not give a freshly activated Nautilus the helper's Zsh. An already-running app also retains its existing environment. This is a limitation of the new code path, not a failure of the shell lookup. Address D-Bus activation explicitly or narrow the stated guarantee and add a D-Bus-activatable fixture; `gtk-launch` with a mocked executable cannot establish this case.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus obs 3; Nautilus facts verified (omarchy-base.packages, desktop entry); published as behaviour note

leads.summary: Coordinate the competing AppLibrary launch paths with open #10570
leads.consequence: #10570 switches Apps to `uwsm-app -t service -- gtk-launch` to consume the user manager's newly synchronized GDK_SCALE. This PR replaces precisely that invocation with a helper that calls `uwsm-app --` without -t. Git's three-way merge conflicts on the invocation and both app-search assertions; choosing this PR's line drops #10570's service launch and its scale fix, while choosing #10570's line drops this PR's shell fix. A combined implementation must retain `-t service` in the actual helper-to-UWSM call and the shell override inside the launched command, not pass `-t service` as a GTK desktop ID. #10570 is not stacked; GitHub reports it MERGEABLE against its base, which does not resolve this head-to-head collision.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus obs 6; PR open and merge conflict verified; published

leads.summary: Coordinate workspace-pinned launch path with open #9479
leads.consequence: #9479 routes the Apps command through `omarchy-launch-on-workspace` to retain the click-time workspace when a window appears late. Its constructed command still contains the old `uwsm-app -- gtk-launch` path, so resolving the same-line merge in its favor loses this PR's login-shell refresh; taking only this PR's line loses workspace pinning. Its app-search assertion independently requires its wrapper and old command. Both overlapping files yield conflict markers in a merge against this head. A combined solution could pass a properly quoted invocation of this helper to the workspace wrapper and update both assertions. #9479 is not stacked and GitHub reports CONFLICTING against its base.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus obs 6; wrapper line verified in gh pr diff; published

leads.summary: Coordinate monitored launch and failure feedback with open #8978
leads.consequence: #8978 replaces detached execution with a monitored Quickshell Process that notifies on a failed gtk-launch. Its `launchProcess.command` still executes `uwsm-app -- gtk-launch` without this helper. The three-way merge has conflicts at this invocation and both tests: taking #8978's path loses refreshed SHELL, taking only this PR's detached path leaves #8978's monitor unused (and launch failure remains silent). Resolve by having its Process invoke the helper, and account for service-mode's asynchronous exit separately. #8978 is not stacked; GitHub reports it MERGEABLE against its base.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus obs 6; PR open verified; published

leads.summary: The Apps integration assertion passes when the UI still launches without the helper
leads.consequence: The test checks for text anywhere in launch() and an include anywhere in the QML, not the executable expression. A plausible stale comment naming the helper alongside the preexisting direct uwsm-app invocation makes all assertions pass while every Apps click keeps its old SHELL; the new shell-script test invokes the helper directly and therefore cannot catch a disconnected UI. Add an assertion over the actual execDetached call expression or exercise the QML launch through a stubbed command/process. Without it a future reversion of the wiring can silently pass the suite.
leads.triage: dropped: contrived mutation, source-grep test style predates PR

leads.summary: The failure-propagation fixture models synchronous scope execution, not service launches
leads.consequence: The service-mode stub first replaces SHELL but then directly execs gtk-launch. Its exit-17 assertion is not in service mode, and it would incorrectly ascribe GTK's post-start failure status to a real service launch. UWSM invokes systemd-run without --wait for service, which starts asynchronously; a GTK failure after start cannot reach the helper's exit code. The test's advertised 'desktop launch failure is reported' is therefore only true for the synchronous scope path, and the Apps UI itself uses detached execution and does not observe that status. Assert the scope-only contract and add an explicit asynchronous service fixture if service error reporting is expected. This is a test-fidelity gap, not proof the new helper newly broke service status.
leads.triage: used as qualifier only: exit-status claim limited to scope mode; verified UWSM builds systemd-run without --wait for service; no finding

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in stubbed tests and in the UWSM, systemd and GLib source, the new `omarchy-launch-desktop` helper gives the app the account's current passwd shell in both UWSM scope and service mode. Desktop IDs reach `gtk-launch` exactly as before, and URI arguments pass through unchanged. No functional defect was found in the tested scope. The notes below cover scope boundaries, one small test gap and overlapping open PRs.

| Apps launch, caller has stale `SHELL=/bin/bash`, passwd shell is zsh (stubbed) | Merge base | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| UWSM scope mode | `/bin/bash` | passwd shell |
| UWSM service mode (manager environment only) | `/bin/bash` | passwd shell |
| Lookup fails, shell missing, empty or relative | inherited `SHELL` | inherited `SHELL` (unchanged launch) |

**Verified details:**
- The change to `AppLibrary.qml` still goes through `Util.shellQuote` and `Util.execDetached`, so quoting is as safe as before. IDs with spaces, `org.telegram.desktop` (an ID that itself ends in `.desktop`, which reaches `gtk-launch` as `org.telegram.desktop.desktop`, as on the merge base) and an ID containing `$(...)`, backticks and `;` each reached `gtk-launch` as one exact argument, and nothing in them was executed.
- Setting `SHELL` inside the `uwsm-app` command (commit c65c5d4) is what makes service mode work: UWSM's service mode passes only the XDG seat/session variables with `--setenv`, so the service otherwise starts with the user manager's environment. That environment has `SHELL` fixed from passwd when the user manager starts, which confirms the stale-shell premise.
- The launch's exit status reaches the caller in scope mode (a `gtk-launch` exit of 17 and a `uwsm-app` exit of 3, with stubs). In service mode UWSM starts the unit without waiting, so only the start status comes back, as before.
- `getent passwd <uid> | cut -d: -f7` always yields the shell field: glibc's `putpwent` rejects colons in every field except GECOS and rewrites them there.
- `desktop-login-shell-test.sh`, `app-search-test.sh` and `desktop-entry-launch-test.sh` pass on the head and on the head merged onto the current `quattro` tip, and `omarchy commands --check` passes. On the merge base, the updated `app-search-test.sh` fails as expected.

### Other launch paths still pass the stale shell

Only the Apps menu (`AppLibrary.qml:85`) uses the helper. Nine lines in eight scripts on `quattro` still run `setsid uwsm-app -- gtk-launch` directly, including `bin/omarchy-install-ai-t3-code:28` (T3 Code, the app named in the PR) and `bin/omarchy-install-and-launch:27`, which serves the menu's install-and-launch entries. Keybinding and terminal launches are unchanged too. The PR description says other launch paths are out of scope.

**Impact:** after `chsh` in the same session, T3 Code launched from Apps gets the new shell, but T3 Code launched right after installing it from the menu still gets the stale one.

**Suggested change:** switch these call sites to `omarchy-launch-desktop`, here or in a follow-up. `test/shell.d/desktop-entry-launch-test.sh:67-69`, `:85` and `:93` assert the literal `uwsm-app -- gtk-launch` commands and would need to change with them.

### Behaviour notes for maintainers

- **A deliberately set `SHELL` is overridden for Apps launches.** A `SHELL` set without `chsh` (for example through `environment.d` or a compositor environment setting) now loses to the passwd shell for Apps launches only, while every other launch path keeps it. The PR calls the login shell "authoritative", so this is intended. How often such setups occur is unknown.
- **D-Bus-activated apps do not receive the new `SHELL`.** GIO starts entries with `DBusActivatable=true` over the session bus instead of spawning them, so the `SHELL` set on `gtk-launch` never reaches the process. Nautilus, installed by default, is such an entry. Already running single-instance apps are also unaffected. Behaviour matches the merge base for these apps, so this is a limit of the fix, not a regression.

**Optional test improvement:** no test case uses a relative shell path, so removing the `$login_shell == /*` check leaves `desktop-login-shell-test.sh` passing (a surviving mutation). The case needs a relative path that points to an existing executable from the helper's working directory, because `-x` resolves it there. For example, `(cd "$scratch" && PASSWD_SHELL=bin/gtk-launch SHELL=/bin/bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-desktop" example.desktop)` should keep `/bin/bash`; it passes with the current helper and fails once the check is removed.

**Overlapping open PRs:** #8978 (failed-launch reporting), #10570 (`uwsm-app -t service` for GDK_SCALE sync) and #9479 (workspace pinning) each rewrite the same `AppLibrary.qml` launch line, and a three-way merge of each with this PR conflicts there and in `app-search-test.sh`. Their goals are compatible, so whichever merges later has to keep both behaviours. In particular, #9479's wrapper still contains the direct `uwsm-app -- gtk-launch` command.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the PR against the merge base and the current `quattro` tip, plus UWSM v0.27.0, GLib, GTK3 `gtk-launch`, glibc, systemd, foot, Nautilus and T3 Code source (current upstream, not necessarily the exact Arch package versions). Isolated command-only runs used stubbed `getent`, `uwsm-app` and `gtk-launch`, with the service-mode stub keeping only a manager environment. No real UWSM, systemd, D-Bus or desktop launches were made, so the author's live test was not reproduced. The full `./test/all` suite was not run, so the reported unrelated failures were not checked.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
